note.note:
ENT Clinical Note – Telemedicine Visit  

Subjective:
• Presenting complaint: 1-week history of sore throat followed 1–2 days later by a dry, non-productive cough. No clear trigger or exposure identified.  
• Symptom timeline/progression:  
  – Day 0–1: Sore throat began (Thu/Fri last week).  
  – Day 1–2: Dry cough appeared.  
  – Day 3–4: Developed mild exertional shortness of breath, occasional wheeze, mild chest discomfort.  
  – First 3 days: Subjective low-grade fever; now afebrile.  
  – Intermittent headaches; variable (“up-and-down”) overall course; appetite reduced but no weight loss.  
• ENT-related symptoms:  
  – Throat: Sore throat; no sensation of throat closing; no dysphagia, odynophagia, drooling, or voice change.  
  – Nasal/ocular: Denies congestion, rhinorrhea, sinus pressure, or ocular symptoms.  
  – Airway/respiratory: Dry cough; exertional dyspnea; reports wheeze; no stridor or noisy breathing at rest.  
  – Swelling: No facial, lip, tongue, or neck swelling reported.  
  – Ear/neck: No ear pain, hearing change, neck pain, or palpable neck masses.  
• Past episodes/treatments: None; no prior similar illnesses requiring ED or epinephrine.  
• Past medical history: Denies chronic illnesses, asthma, thromboembolic disease.  
• Allergies: Peanut (reaction details not discussed).  
• Current medications: None.  
• Social context: Non-smoker; no asbestos exposure; lives/work in UK; missed 2 workdays and requests sick note.  

Objective:
• Visible swelling: None reported/observed via video.  
• Airway/breathing: Speaking in full sentences; exertional dyspnea only; no visible distress on camera.  
• Mental status: Alert, oriented; no dizziness or syncope reported.  
• Vitals/exam: Not recorded (remote consult).  
• Accompaniment: Not specified.

Assessment:
Working impression: Likely acute viral upper respiratory infection / viral bronchitis.  
Evidence: Typical 1-week viral prodrome (sore throat → dry cough, low-grade fever, improving trend). Exertional wheeze and SOB mild without red-flag airway findings.  
DDx reference (top aligned items):  
1. Acute viral URI / viral bronchitis – high likelihood (see above).  
2. COVID-19 infection – moderate likelihood; similar symptom cluster (sore throat, dry cough, fever, headache, appetite loss); no anosmia reported, currently improving.  
3. Reactive airway disease/new-onset asthma – consider if wheeze persists post-viral; no past asthma history.  
No evidence for anaphylaxis, bacterial tonsillitis, or ENT abscess. DDx and transcript consistent; no conflicts noted.

Plan:
• Symptomatic management: Paracetamol (acetaminophen) as needed for throat discomfort, headache, and fever. Encourage adequate oral hydration and rest.  
• Work accommodation: Electronic sick note provided for additional days off work.  
• Self-monitoring / escalation: Seek in-person medical review (GP or urgent care) if any of the following occur:  
  – Worsening or new shortness of breath, wheeze, or chest pain.  
  – Development of high fever, purulent sputum, haemoptysis, or inability to swallow.  
  – Onset of throat tightness, stridor, facial/lip/tongue swelling, or voice change (airway red flags).  
• COVID-19 considerations: Advised to obtain COVID-19 testing if symptoms persist or worsen, per local guidelines; isolate according to public-health advice if positive.  
• Follow-up: Expect gradual improvement over next 4–5 days. If no improvement or any red flags, attend face-to-face GP assessment or emergency services. Consider spirometry or peak-flow measurement if cough/wheeze persist beyond acute phase to evaluate for asthma.  
• Education: Reassured low likelihood of TB or lung cancer given acute onset and improving course; advised return for further evaluation if constitutional or respiratory symptoms persist >3 weeks.

Quality checks (document_quality):
● Missing elements: No vital signs, throat or chest examination, COVID-19 test result, detailed peanut-allergy reaction history, medication dose/frequency, vaccination status, history of prior similar URIs.  
● Transcript-DDx conflicts: None identified.  
● Transcript quality: Clear audio; minor conversational overlaps but clinically adequate information captured.
